final_answer:
Let
\[
F_N(a)=S_1(N,a).
\]
Using
\[
S_1(N,a)=\int_0^1 x^{a-1}(1-x)^N\,dx
=\frac{\Gamma(a)\Gamma(N+1)}{\Gamma(N+a+1)},
\]
we have
\[
S_2(N,a)=-\frac{\partial}{\partial a}S_1(N,a)
=S_1(N,a)\bigl(\psi(N+a+1)-\psi(a)\bigr).
\]
Write
\[
H_N(a)=\psi(N+a+1)-\psi(a).
\]

The determinant condition says the weighted average of \(H_N\) in \(T\) equals the corresponding weighted average in \(U\). Since \(T\) and \(U\) differ only in the \(n^3\)-term, this is equivalent to
\[
\frac{\Delta(FH)}{\Delta F}
=
\frac{\sum_{q=1}^3 e^{q-1}F_{n^q}H_{n^q}}
{\sum_{q=1}^3 e^{q-1}F_{n^q}},
\]
where
\[
\Delta F=e^2\left(p_nF_{n^3+m_n}+(1-p_n)F_{n^3+n^2}-F_{n^3}\right).
\]

Put
\[
x=aL.
\]
We need \(x=1+o(1)\). For \(N=n^q\),
\[
F_N(a)=\Gamma(a)N^{-a}\left(1-\frac{a(a+1)}{2N}+O(N^{-2})\right),
\]
and
\[
H_N(a)=\log N-\psi(a)+\frac{a+1/2}{N}+O(N^{-2}).
\]

For the \(T\)-average, at \(x=1\) the three main weights are equal because
\[
e^{q-1}n^{-qa}=e^{q-1-q}=e^{-1}.
\]
Only the \(q=1\) correction contributes at order \(1/n\). Thus
\[
\frac1L\left(
\frac{\sum e^{q-1}F_{n^q}H_{n^q}}{\sum e^{q-1}F_{n^q}}
-H_{n^3}
\right)
=
-1+\frac1n\left(\frac1{3L}+\frac1{2L^2}\right)
-\frac23(x-1)+o\!\left(\frac1{nL^3}\right).
\]

Now consider the perturbation in \(U\). For \(s\in\{1/3,1\}\),
\[
n^3+s n^2=n^3(1+s/n),
\]
and
\[
\frac{F_{n^3+sn^2}}{F_{n^3}}
=
\exp\left(-a\log(1+s/n)\right)+O(n^{-2}).
\]
Let
\[
z_s=\frac{\log(1+s/n)}{L}.
\]
Then
\[
\frac1L\left(\frac{\Delta(FH)}{\Delta F}-H_{n^3}\right)
=
\frac{p_ne^{-xz_{1/3}}z_{1/3}+(1-p_n)e^{-xz_1}z_1}
{p_ne^{-xz_{1/3}}+(1-p_n)e^{-xz_1}-1}
+o\!\left(\frac1{nL^3}\right).
\]
Expanding in \(z_s=O(1/(nL))\),
\[
= -\frac1x+\frac12\frac{p_nz_{1/3}^2+(1-p_n)z_1^2}
{p_nz_{1/3}+(1-p_n)z_1}
+o\!\left(\frac1{nL^3}\right).
\]
Since \(z_s=s/(nL)+O(n^{-2})\),
\[
\frac{p_nz_{1/3}^2+(1-p_n)z_1^2}
{p_nz_{1/3}+(1-p_n)z_1}
=
\frac1{nL}
\frac{p_n/9+(1-p_n)}{p_n/3+(1-p_n)}
+O(n^{-2}).
\]
Using
\[
p_n=\frac34-\frac{9}{8L},
\]
one gets
\[
\frac{p_n/9+(1-p_n)}{p_n/3+(1-p_n)}
=
\frac{4(L+3)}{3(2L+3)}
=
\frac23+\frac1L-\frac{3}{2L^2}+O(L^{-3}).
\]
Therefore the \(U\)-side equals
\[
-1+(x-1)
+\frac1n\left(\frac1{3L}+\frac1{2L^2}-\frac{3}{4L^3}\right)
+o\!\left(\frac1{nL^3}\right).
\]

Equating the two sides gives
\[
-1+(x-1)+\frac1n\left(\frac1{3L}+\frac1{2L^2}-\frac{3}{4L^3}\right)
=
-1-\frac23(x-1)+\frac1n\left(\frac1{3L}+\frac1{2L^2}\right)
+o\!\left(\frac1{nL^3}\right).
\]
Hence
\[
\frac53(x-1)=\frac{3}{4nL^3}+o\!\left(\frac1{nL^3}\right),
\]
so
\[
x-1=a_nL-1=\frac{9}{20nL^3}+o\!\left(\frac1{nL^3}\right).
\]

Thus
\[
\boxed{\lim_{n\to\infty} nL^3(a_nL-1)=\frac{9}{20}}.
\]
